summary.name: Swift Shift
summary.one_liner: Swift Shift is a free, open-source macOS utility for moving and resizing windows with the mouse or keyboard shortcuts.
use_cases: Move windows with the mouse without hunting for title bars
Resize windows from the nearest corner or edge
Set keyboard shortcuts for window placement
Use mouse buttons to move and resize windows like on some Linux distros
summary.what_it_does: Swift Shift runs in the background on macOS and lets you move and resize windows by holding modifier keys and dragging with the mouse, without needing to target small arrows or title bars. You can set up keyboard shortcuts to move and resize windows. It can include mouse buttons in its shortcuts. By default it resizes from the bottom-right corner, and an optional quadrants mode resizes from whichever edge or corner is closest to the mouse. It can launch at login and hide its menubar icon.
notable: Quadrants mode resizes from the edge or corner nearest the mouse
Mouse buttons can be included in shortcuts
Open source with code on GitHub
Runs in background with optional hidden menubar icon
caveats: Only available for macOS, as far as the page states
The page does not describe paid tiers, so pricing is stated only as open source and freeware per the listing
